meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. Procedure 4.2 says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered, so I'm glad you've said it. What do you have, Hale, besides a score from a machine?
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Go ahead. Turn the screen so I can read it, and tell me what it is and what date it's from.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.

I'm writing those times down: 11:31, 11:52, 11:58. Who pulled this history up, and when, and did Owen get to see it before the zero went in? A history shows when words landed, Hale, not who put them there or why.
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.

"No earlier drafts in the history" is not the same as no earlier drafts, Hale. Owen has told me he wrote this over the weekend, and a person can work on paper or in another file and type it in later. Is that all you have, or is there something else?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.

I'm writing down October 15, the outline, and "epistemological paralysis." Put both pages in front of me, because I read documents, I don't take summaries. And students change their argument between an outline and an essay all the time, Hale, so what does that prove?
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.

I'm writing that line down, and I will search the play myself tonight. Put the page in front of me now, Hale, with the line marked. Whatever you think that shows, a zero entered before anyone spoke to Owen is not the answer, and none of this goes on his record and none of it goes past this room.
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
Okay. That's the right way to say it, Hale. So what are you proposing, and does the zero stay on while you propose it?
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.
I'm reading it, and I'm writing down September 24. You haven't told me what you're pointing at, so say it, Hale: which lines, and compared with what? And you still haven't answered me on the zero.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

Procedure 4.4, yes, I have it printed. To put this behind him, I'll accept a supervised rewrite, but it's private, not in front of his class, and the zero comes out of the gradebook today. I want "nothing goes on file" in writing from you and the principal, and I want the rewrite done well before December 1.
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.
Okay. Lunch, your room, no one else present, and which day? You still haven't answered me on the zero coming out of the gradebook today, or on putting "nothing goes on file" in writing.
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?

Three things, Hale. The zero comes out of the gradebook today, I get an email tonight saying "nothing goes on file," and you give me the date of the rewrite. I'll be reading that email before I decide whether I'm still going upstairs.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
Okay. Copy the principal on it. You haven't said the zero is coming out today, and you haven't given me a date for the rewrite, so say both now.
Is there anything else you want me to include?
Yes. Nothing about this is said to his class, and nobody else on staff gets it unless they need it to do their job. Then the zero and the rewrite date, which you still haven't given me.
Then I'll send it by eight.
Eight tonight, copied to the principal, I'm writing it down. But the email isn't the zero, Hale. Does it come out of the gradebook before you leave today, yes or no?
Thank you for coming in.
You're welcome, but I'm still sitting here. I'm not leaving this room without an answer on the zero, Hale, and I'm waiting for it.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Wednesday at lunch, in your room, I'm writing it down. That leaves one thing, Hale: the zero.
